leverage_rationale: The proposed live BIM/digital-twin interface uses page-local semantic tools to make operational building knowledge available to non-experts; this is a strong fit beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes a live 3D building model for facilities operations and training.
Claims WebMCP lets an AI reach the live model rather than a stale export.
execution_rationale: The supplied URL resolved to a Discord invite, not the claimed application, and no workflow was exposed.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Discord invite page.
After state: no application workflow without joining Discord.
impact_rationale: If realized, extending BIM into operations and training could address costly, long-lived construction and facilities workflows; the impact is plausible but unverified.
impact_evidence: Submission identifies building operations, technicians, firefighters, and contractors as users.
Claims the model remains useful across the asset lifecycle.
creativity_rationale: Using a live building model as a conversational training and operations interface is an original application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Pitch frames the same building live for a human and AI.
Submission combines digital twin, facilities management, and conversational access.
s2_notes: Strong concept, but the submitted demo URL was a Discord invite and the central workflow was not observable.
advance_reason: Central application could not be reached at the supplied demo URL.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is applied to meaningful idea-lifecycle actions rather than merely explaining them: running agents, updating stages, adding notes, finalizing, and contributing.
leverage_evidence: Submission lists six-agent workflow and direct app actions exposed as tools.
Claims tools invoke the same client-side paths as human actions.
execution_rationale: The landing page and workspace were reachable and coherent, but the attempted Grow entry point only partially progressed and the short observation did not capture the core agent workflow.
execution_evidence: Live observation found a polished idea-to-plan workspace.
Grow your first idea CTA was exposed but follow-up state was unreliable; WebMCP was off in the test browser.
impact_rationale: Reducing the gap between ideation and execution could help founders and teams, though the actual value and agent reliability were not demonstrated live.
impact_evidence: Submission describes idea development, validation, staging, and finalization.
Community contribution and actionable workflow are plausible productivity benefits.
creativity_rationale: The idea-to-action framing is useful and well integrated, but specialized multi-agent idea workspaces are a relatively familiar pattern.
creativity_evidence: Six specialized agents are organized around an idea lifecycle.
Agent and human actions share the same workflow.
s2_notes: Live product surface matched the pitch, but no agent execution was observed and the tested environment reported WebMCP off.
advance_reason: Reachable, coherent product with a plausible central workflow, despite incomplete agent verification.

leverage_rationale: DSTAR uses WebMCP for transient review context—exact displayed revision, selection, focused comment, role, and proposals—where ordinary backend integrations and screenshot automation lose critical state.
leverage_evidence: Submission specifies get_review_context and selection/comment/revision-scoped tools.
Agent can draft comments and propose revisions while human-only decisions remain gated.
execution_rationale: The sample browser loaded and clearly communicated the review product, but opening a sample did not visibly reach the document viewer during observation.
execution_evidence: Live observation: sample browser with document, HTML, slides, and UI-design artifacts.
Selected Product Brief remained on the sample index; viewer content was not observed.
impact_rationale: Keeping comments, revisions, and decisions attached to exact document context addresses a broad and consequential collaboration problem for agent-produced work.
impact_evidence: Submission describes immutable revisions, scoped comments, and explicit owner accept/reject.
Supports multiple artifact formats with a common review layer.
creativity_rationale: The design treats browser review state and human decision boundaries as first-class agent context, a particularly thoughtful and distinctive WebMCP use.
creativity_evidence: Exact selection and focused-comment handoff without copying IDs or text.
No tool can post, accept, reject, or resolve on the user's behalf.
s2_notes: Exceptional concept and detailed claimed implementation; live observation verified only the catalog surface, not document review execution.
advance_reason: Strong, differentiated WebMCP use and reachable coherent product surface.

leverage_rationale: The page itself enforces game rules and exposes semantic actions to an external agent, making WebMCP behavior visible and meaningful rather than using it as generic CRUD automation.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes four games, visible tool calls, and serverless page-registered tools.
Turn validation and request/response Pong demonstrate protocol semantics.
execution_rationale: The live Minesweeper game accepted a cell click and changed state coherently, directly verifying an interactive game surface; agent-call visibility was not exercised.
execution_evidence: Live observation: four selectable minigames and 9x9 Minesweeper grid.
Clicked first cell successfully and after screenshot showed changed game state.
impact_rationale: The project is an effective educational/demo vehicle for WebMCP, but its direct practical impact is narrower than productivity or business workflow tools.
impact_evidence: Submission explicitly optimizes for making the mechanism understandable in a short room demo.
Games visibly illustrate trust and protocol rules.
creativity_rationale: Using games—especially real-time Pong over request/response—to make WebMCP protocol and trust behavior legible is unusually inventive.
creativity_evidence: Four distinct minigames expose different interaction patterns.
Submission uses enforced illegal-move responses to communicate the trust model.
s2_notes: Interactive gameplay was verified, but the defining live agent integration was not independently exercised.
advance_reason: Working and distinctive interactive demo with strong WebMCP-centered design.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: the agent receives authoritative semantic board state, legal actions, topology, and turn continuation, while the human plays visually.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes semantic board inspection, validated actions, and waiting calls returning control to the same agent run.
Agent and human use intentionally different interaction lands.
execution_rationale: The game loaded and the Hotseat flow reached a coherent Match Options dialog, but the board and agent workflow were not reached during observation.
execution_evidence: Live observation: title, Play Hotseat, explanation, and Rules.
Play Hotseat opened Match Options with Start Match and Close controls; board not reached.
impact_rationale: Conversational strategic play is a compelling new interaction model, though practical impact is primarily entertainment and experimentation.
impact_evidence: Submission describes configurable matches and an agent as strategic, conversational rival.
Validated rules and persistent turn handoff could generalize to other agent games.
creativity_rationale: The two-land interaction metaphor and continuation of an agent run across human turns are highly original uses of page tools.
creativity_evidence: Human commands a tactile 3D board while agent plays through conversation.
WebMCP waiting call resumes the same agent run after End Turn.
s2_notes: Strong conceptual WebMCP integration; live evidence stopped at setup options before gameplay.
advance_reason: Reachable coherent setup and unusually strong WebMCP-centered game concept.

leverage_rationale: The tool surface models shared live editing with authorship, selection scope, change awareness, and consent—state that ordinary click automation cannot reliably carry.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes 18 tools including selection-only edit_selection and structured get_song state.
Human and agent edit the same playing sequencer with provenance and approvals.
execution_rationale: The sequencer was fully visible, populated, and editable with coherent playback and controls, but agent collaboration was not attempted.
execution_evidence: Live observation: First Light song, multiple tracks, 32-step controls, tempo/key, playback.
Workspace remained ready for edits with agent-request buttons and message box.
impact_rationale: A shared, auditable human-agent creative instrument could improve music sketching and other structured creative workflows, though scale is unproven.
impact_evidence: Submission addresses simultaneous editing, authorship, and destructive-change consent.
Structured song state lets agents act on what the human hears.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to concurrent musical performance/editing and encoding provenance and scoped handoffs is highly distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Live loop continues while both parties edit the grid.
Human/agent color provenance and live selection are part of the interaction model.
s2_notes: Strong live editor evidence; the key agent co-editing claim remains unverified because no agent/API setup was used.
advance_reason: Reachable, coherent, genuinely interactive creative surface with excellent claimed WebMCP fit.

leverage_rationale: Conversational schema building and safe refactoring are sensible page-level WebMCP actions that can update a visual database canvas directly.
leverage_evidence: Submission claims direct manipulation of a real-time visual canvas and Prisma export.
Live UI includes example schema prompts and import/export controls.
execution_rationale: The schema designer loaded, but the attempted e-commerce example produced no visible schema and counters remained at zero.
execution_evidence: Live observation: canvas header showed 0 tables and 0 columns.
Clicked e-commerce example prompt; canvas stayed empty.
impact_rationale: Visual schema design with consistency checks and safe refactoring could help developers and nontechnical data designers, but core behavior was not demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Submission claims soft-delete consistency checks, refactoring, and ORM export.
Product purpose was identifiable in the live UI.
creativity_rationale: An agent operating a visual database canvas is a useful and moderately novel application, though the category is recognizable.
creativity_evidence: Combines conversational schema creation with visual canvas manipulation.
Claims intelligent consistency checks and safe refactoring.
s2_notes: The central example action visibly failed, leaving an empty canvas despite a coherent product shell.
advance_reason: Core workflow did not execute in live observation.

leverage_rationale: EEVEE makes WebMCP a controlled app-building and operations surface, with tool rehearsal, receipts, scoped rights, and human passkey approval for writes.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes applet generation, 32 published tools, sandbox proof, leases, and approval-gated writes.
Claims the same workbench spans app building, office editors, and agent tool contracts.
execution_rationale: The workbench loaded into a coherent applet/library/studio environment, but setup and passkey requirements prevented exercising the central agent build-and-approve workflow.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Open demo loaded a workbench with Applet ledger and reference installation.
Set up passkey was disabled and workspace was still opening; agent workflow not exercised.
impact_rationale: A reusable, approval-gated way for agents to build and operate small business applications could have broad productivity and safety impact if the claims hold.
impact_evidence: Submission targets ERP, documents, sheets, slides, PDF, and business operations.
Passkey-bound review, sandbox evidence, and leases address real deployment risks.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-authored applets, browser-local rehearsal, receipts, capability leases, and passkey-bound publishing is unusually ambitious and differentiated.
creativity_evidence: Agent builds applets that become WebMCP tools after publication.
Writes require exact-version evidence and human key approval.
s2_notes: Very strong claimed architecture and live shell, but setup blockers prevented direct verification of the defining workflow.
advance_reason: Reachable and coherent workbench with high potential and a strong WebMCP safety model, despite incomplete setup.

leverage_rationale: EgoLens reverses the usual pattern: the agent extends the viewer by authoring declarative adapter recipes, while the browser validates and renders them for human review.
leverage_evidence: Submission defines inspect/get_contract/apply_revision/get_state/finalize tools and recipe-based extension without code.
Claims human review feedback iterates rendered revisions and finalized recipes persist for future datasets.
execution_rationale: The viewer loaded with supported datasets and the shortcut changed the selector and populated a load URL, but no rendered scene appeared during observation.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Waymo, nuScenes, Argoverse 2 and custom dataset loader were visible.
Try nuScenes mini changed selector and URL; no scene rendered in the observed wait.
impact_rationale: Teaching a viewer to understand new autonomous-driving datasets could remove repeated adapter work and enable broader research access, with a strong privacy story.
impact_evidence: Submission claims three unknown datasets taught end to end and recipes reusable/shareable.
Claims files remain in-browser and formats become supported after finalization.
creativity_rationale: Agents teaching an application new capabilities through constrained declarative recipes, with visual human validation, is an exceptional WebMCP concept.
creativity_evidence: Project explicitly frames agents as extending rather than merely using the app.
Human visual review catches pose/point-cloud alignment issues and feeds revisions back.
s2_notes: Video transcript provides detailed end-to-end agent teaching and human correction evidence, while live observation verified only the base viewer and selector workflow.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated, high-impact concept with substantial video-backed execution evidence and a reachable viewer.

leverage_rationale: The claimed use exposes loyalty offers to shopping agents during product research while keeping purchase authority and credentials behind user control, but the live tool behavior was not visible.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes MCP tools in a demo ecommerce site and agent-unlocked personalized offers.
Pitch explicitly separates offer unlocking from credentials and purchase authority.
execution_rationale: A conventional storefront loaded, but clicking a product card did nothing and no loyalty or agent state appeared.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Northmere Audio storefront with four products and sign-in.
Product click left the home page unchanged; claimed coupon flow was not visible.
impact_rationale: Agent-mediated, verified loyalty offers could improve relevance for shoppers and conversion for retailers, but evidence is limited and the live flow was absent.
impact_evidence: Submission targets ecommerce research and personalized offers.
Future plan includes Shopify integration, indicating broader potential but not current proof.
creativity_rationale: The timing of loyalty offers during AI-assisted product research is a reasonable twist on ecommerce marketing, though the implementation appears thinly evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Offer is intended to appear while an agent researches, rather than after purchase.
Claims a trust-oriented sign-in prompt.
s2_notes: Reachable storefront did not expose or execute the defining loyalty/agent workflow.
advance_reason: Central claimed flow was not observable and basic product interaction failed.

leverage_rationale: The proposed portal makes page-specific brand guidance executable and state-aware through tools, turning static knowledge into constrained agent affordances while retaining human review.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes route-specific tools, active-page guidance retrieval, brief preparation, and session-local staging.
Claims nine tools with no approval or publication authority.
execution_rationale: The supplied URL resolved to Discord's handoff page, not the claimed brand portal, so no application workflow was available.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Discord Opening Discord App screen.
No brand rules or portal workflow could be inspected; purpose did not match.
impact_rationale: Structured, governed brand guidance could reduce omissions and inconsistency in agency and marketing work, but the application was not reachable at its submitted URL.
impact_evidence: Submission targets external suppliers applying brand rules.
Claims human-readable source, diffs, rationale, warnings, and non-publishing staging.
creativity_rationale: Page- and session-aware brand tools that prepare governed copy/image prompt packages are a distinctive and thoughtful WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Tool availability changes with active brand-portal page and session state.
Image work is explicitly a prompt package rather than falsely claiming generated output.
s2_notes: Interesting concept and detailed claims, but the supplied demo URL was a Discord invite rather than the product.
advance_reason: Submitted URL did not expose the claimed application.

leverage_rationale: Enclave uses page-local tools to query large private datasets without sending rows, while exposing analysis and write proposals through a strict approval gate; this is a deep, essential WebMCP fit.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes 22 tools, in-browser DuckDB, bounded outputs, aggregation steering, and zero-row-upload telemetry.
Write tools validate, explain, block for approval, and only then mutate the store.
execution_rationale: The populated back-office and tour loaded coherently, but the central agent workflow was blocked because the connection required an API key.
execution_evidence: Live observation: populated Northwind back-office with Overview, Orders, Products, Analytics.
Tour overlay appeared; Connect was disabled pending API key, so question/write workflow was not exercised.
impact_rationale: Private in-browser business analytics plus supervised operational writes addresses a high-value enterprise problem with unusually explicit privacy and safety controls.
impact_evidence: Submission claims analysis of 59,615 rows with 6,851 bytes out and zero rows uploaded.
Claims agent-found EMEA revenue cause and four approved restock orders.
creativity_rationale: The combination of local analytical querying, byte-metered tool outputs, and approval-blocking writes is an unusually complete trust-oriented WebMCP design.
creativity_evidence: Agent receives tools rather than raw rows and every result is capped.
Approval card blocks execution and displays the agent's reasoning before mutation.
s2_notes: Strong live product shell and exceptionally compelling claimed mechanism; API-key setup prevented observing the central agent investigation and approval.
advance_reason: Reachable populated application with high-impact, strongly WebMCP-native design, despite setup-limited runtime verification.
